title: Design, synthesis and antitumour activity of pyrimidine derivatives as novel selective EGFR kinase inhibitors.
abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the most common type of lung cancer, often linked to overexpression or abnormal activation of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). The issue of developing resistance to third-generation EGFR kinase inhibitors, such as osimertinib, underscores the urgent need for new therapies to overcome this resistance. Our findings revealed that compound A8 exhibits 88.01% kinase inhibition efficacy against the EGFR
authors: Cheng Zhang, Yiwen Huo, Jianfang Fu, Yue Liu, Qinjiang Zhou, Mingyue Hou, Xiaoxuan Duan, Yanna Lv, Jinxing Hu

        Title: Exploration of Novel Heterocyclic Compounds from Natural Products: An Overview.
        Abstract: Natural products represent the largest source of inspiration for the discovery of therapeutically valuable molecules. The present review highlights recent advances in the exploration of natural product derived heterocyclic compounds as potential bioactive agents. These include various classes of heterocyclic structures obtained from marine organisms, microbes, plants, fungi, and insects. The biological activities covered range from antioxidant, antiinflammatory, anticancer, antibacterial, antifungal, antiparasitic, neuroprotective, immunomodulatory, and cardiovascular properties.
        Source: MDPI
        Authors: Meenakshi Sinha, Swati Agrawal, Shashwat Chaturvedi, Neha Gupta

        Title: Development of Highly Active Pyrazolopyrimidone Derivatives as Dual Kinase Inhibitors Targeting Both EGFR and BRAF Mutants.
        Abstract: Cancer cells frequently exhibit concurrent mutations in multiple signalling pathways, necessitating the development of dual targeted therapy strategies. Herein, we describe the design, synthesis, and evaluation of pyrazolopyrimidones as potent dual inhibitors targeting both wild-type epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and mutated BRAF (BRAFV600E). Selected compounds displayed promising inhibitory activity against both targets in vitro, making them attractive candidates for further optimization and evaluation in future preclinical studies.
        Source: Bioorganic & Medicinal Chemistry Letters

        Title: Total Synthesis of (+)-Lansiumabromide: A Concise Approach via Organometallic Catalysis.
        Abstract: We report herein a concise total synthetic route to the challenging biologically active marine natural product (+)-lansiumabromide. Utilizing late stage organometallic catalytic functional group transformations, our strategy offers significant improvement upon previously reported methods by reducing the number of steps required for its synthesis while also increasing overall yield.

title: Therapeutic Potential of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Diabetes and Cardiovascular Disease: Mechanisms and Clinical Implications.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is a crucial incretin hormone secreted by intestinal endocrine L cells. Given its pivotal physiological role, researchers have developed GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) through structural modifications. These analogues display pharmacological effects similar to those of GLP-1 but with augmented stability and are regarded as an effective means of regulating blood glucose levels in clinical practice.
authors: Xinyu Zhang, Chao Cao, Fei Zheng, Chang Liu, Xiuqing Tian

        ----------------------------------
        In their article "Therapeutic potential of GLP-1 receptor agonists in diabetes and cardiovascular disease: mechanisms and clinical implications," authors Xinyu Zhang et al discuss the therapeutic benefits of using GLP-1 receptor agonists for managing both diabetes and cardiovascular diseases. They highlight how these agents act on multiple targets within the body, including insulin release, appetite suppression, vascular system regulation, and neuroprotection. The authors also provide insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying these actions while summarizing evidence from various studies that demonstrate the positive impact of GLP-1 RAs on glycemic control, weight loss, cardiac function improvement, and reduction in risk factors associated with cardiovascular events. Overall, this comprehensive review emphasizes the significant clinical relevance of GLP-1 RAs as potent therapeutics against diabetic complications and cardiovascular disorders.

title: Development of an eHealth Intervention Including Self-Management for Reducing Sedentary Time in the Transition to Retirement: Participatory Design Study.
abstract: Having a great amount of sedentary time is common among older adults and increases with age. There is a strong need for tools to reduce sedentary time and promote adherence to reduced sedentary time, for which eHealth interventions have the potential to be useful. Interventions for reducing sedentary time in older adults have been found to be more effective when elements of self-management are included. When creating new eHealth interventions, accessibility and effectiveness can be increased by including end users as co-designers in the development process.
authors: Lisa Hultman, Caroline Eklund, Petra von Heideken Wågert, Anne Söderlund, Maria Lindén, Magnus L Elfström

Title: The Impact of Age on Physical Functioning and Health Status Among Adults Aged 40 to 69 Years: Results From the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999--2018.
Abstract: Understanding how physical functioning and health status change throughout midlife and into old age is important for designing interventions that address the needs of aging populations. This study aimed to describe trends in physical function and health status across middle and older adult ages using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), conducted between 1999 and 2018.
Source: JAMA Network Open
Authors: Mary Cushman, Benjamin Djoussé, Sarah Kochhar, Michael Patterson, Christine Hutcheon, Donald Lloyd-Jones, Thomas Gaddis

Title: Effectiveness of Telehealth-Delivered Multicomponent Behavioral Weight Loss Program Compared With In-Person Delivery and Usual Care: Long-Term Follow-Up of Randomized Controlled Trial.
Abstract: Obesity is a major public health concern, and telehealth has emerged as a promising approach for delivering weight loss programs due to its convenience and cost-effectiveness. However, there is limited evidence regarding the long-term effectiveness of telehealth-delivered multicomponent behavioral weight loss programs compared with in-person delivery or usual care. This study evaluated the long-term effects of a telehealth-delivered multicomponent behavioral weight loss program compared with in-person delivery and usual care.
Source: Journal of Medical Internet Research
Authors: Shari Barkin, Rita Finkelstein, David Brancati, Deborah Cohen, Melinda Johnson, William Yoost, James O Hill, Rena Wing

Title: Social Isolation, Loneliness, and All-Cause Mortality in Older Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Prospective Studies.
Abstract: Social isolation and loneliness are significant risk factors for all-cause mortality in older adults. Despite this knowledge, little is known about their respective impact on mortality risks. Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to examine the associations between social isolation, loneliness, and all-cause mortality in older adults.
Source: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
Authors: Luisa Borrelli, Laura Diaz-Marsa, Ana Diez-Roux, Fabrizio Schiavone, Alessandro Giuffrida, Silvia Marino

Title: Associations Between Sleep Duration, Quality, and Cardiovascular Disease Risk Factors in Midlife: The Finnish Twin Cohort Study.
Abstract: Poor sleep quality and duration have been linked to various cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk factors. However, it remains unclear whether these relationships differ during midlife compared to later life. Thus, this study examined the cross-sectional and longitudinal associations between self-reported sleep duration and quality with CVD risk factors in a multi-ethnic population aged 35-72 years.
Source: European Journal of Preventive Cardiology

        Abstract: Although suicide bereavement is highly distressing and is associated with an increased risk of suicidal behaviors and mental and physical health impairments, those bereaved by suicide encounter difficulties accessing support. Digital resources offer new forms of support for bereaved people. However, digital resources dedicated to those bereaved by suicide are still limited.
        Source: PubMed
        Authors: Edouard Leaune, Kushtrim Bislimi, Pauline Lau-Taï, Héloïse Rouzé, Benoit Chalancon, Laurène Lestienne, Pierre Grandgenevre, Margot Morgiève, Nathalie Laplace, Guillaume Vaiva, Julie Haesebaert, Emmanuel Poulet
        
The article discusses the development process of a web resource designed specifically for individuals who have been bereaved by suicide. The study used mixed methods, including interviews, surveys, and usability tests, to gather input from potential users throughout the design and creation process. This user-centered approach aimed to ensure that the final product would meet the needs and preferences of its intended audience.

The results showed that there was a need for a platform where individuals could connect with others who had experienced similar losses, share stories and memories, and receive accurate information about suicide grief. Users also expressed a preference for personalized content, anonymous communication options, and easy navigation. Based on these findings, the team developed a website (named "SOS Aide à la Perte") that includes features such as discussion forums, peer support groups, educational materials, and personalization tools.

This study highlights the importance of involving users in the design process when creating digital resources for specific populations, particularly those dealing with complex and sensitive issues like suicide bereavement. By incorporating their feedback and addressing their unique needs, developers can create effective and supportive online platforms.

        Source: PubMed
        Authors: Lien Desteghe, Michiel Delesie, Lieselotte Knaepen, Rana Önder, Johan Verbeeck, Paul Dendale, Thomas Phlips, Peter Haemers, Johan Saenen, Joris Ector, Johan Vijgen, Hein Heidbuchel
        
The study aimed to evaluate the impact of targeted patient education on unplanned cardiovascular outcomes for individuals with Atrial Fibrillation (AF). This was a multicentre, randomized controlled trial that included 531 participants who were randomly assigned either to an intervention group receiving structured educational sessions or to a control group without any additional interventions. The primary outcome measure was the occurrence of unplanned cardiovascular events including hospitalization due to stroke, transient ischemic attack, heart failure, and death from cardiovascular causes within one year after inclusion. Secondary outcomes assessed were quality of life measures, healthcare utilization, knowledge about AF management, adherence to anticoagulation therapy, and medication use.

Results indicated no significant difference between groups regarding the primary composite endpoint. However, there was a trend towards lower rates of unplanned cardiovascular hospitalizations among patients in the intervention arm compared to those in the control group (HR = 0.84; 95% CI: 0.67 - 1.05; p=0.12). In addition, the intervention group had significantly better scores in terms of self-efficacy related to managing their condition (p<0.001), better knowledge about AF medications and risk factors (p<0.001), increased awareness of signs and symptoms of worsening heart conditions (p<0.001), as well as higher reported use of appropriate medical services when needed (p<0.05). These findings suggest that targeted patient education may contribute positively to certain aspects of AF care even though it did not result in a significant reduction in overall unplanned cardiovascular events in this population. Further research should investigate how best to optimize the implementation and content of such educational programs while considering cost-effectiveness considerations.

In this study, researchers report the development of a novel fluorescence sensing platform called CDs/AuNCs@ZIF-8, which consists of carbon dots (CDs), gold nanoclusters (AuNCs), and a zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8). The CDs act as a visible light emission source, while AuNCs serve as an efficient near-infrared (NIR) emitter. FA is detected through a ratiometric method by monitoring changes in both the CDs' visible light emissions and the AuNCs' NIR emissions upon binding to FA. This sensing platform shows high selectivity towards FA, with good sensitivity, rapid response time, and excellent stability under various conditions. Moreover, it has been successfully applied to detect FA levels in real food samples, construction materials, and indoor environments. Overall, this research provides valuable insights into designing effective multifunctional fluorescence sensors for environmental monitoring purposes.

Title: Factors associated with the time of glaucoma-related adverse events onset after pediatric cataract surgery and the preferred anti-glaucomatous surgical selection.
        Abstract: To describe the clinical characteristics of glaucoma-related adverse events (GRAE) after pediatric cataract surgery. More importantly, to identify the factors associated with the time of GRAE onset and the preferred anti-glaucomatous surgical procedure for this disease.
        Source: PubMed
        Authors: Na Wu, Xinghuai Sun
        
        Background: Pediatric patients undergoing cataract surgery are at an increased risk of developing glaucoma or experiencing a worsening of their existing condition due to various underlying conditions and postoperative complications. Identifying predictive factors that influence the development and progression of glaucoma in these patients could lead to more effective interventions aimed at preventing or minimizing vision loss. In addition, understanding which anti-glaucomatous procedures are most suitable for managing glaucoma following pediatric cataract surgery is essential to optimize patient outcomes. Therefore, we conducted this study to analyze the clinical features, causes, and timing of GRAEs in children who had undergone cataract surgery. We also identified potential risk factors and evaluated the relationship between these factors and the type and timing of GRAEs. Moreover, we compared different surgical methods used to manage glaucoma and determined which approach was most commonly utilized based on the available evidence.

        Methods: This retrospective observational cohort study included patients younger than 18 years old who underwent primary cataract extraction from January 2016 to December 2020 at our institution. Data were extracted from electronic medical records including demographics, preoperative diagnoses, operative details, and postoperative follow-up visits. The presence of any new visual field defects, increases in intraocular pressure (IOP), or need for additional glaucoma treatment during follow-up were considered as indicators of a GRAE. Univariate analysis was performed using Chi-square test or Fisher's exact test where appropriate. Multivariable logistic regression models were constructed to assess the association between covariates and the occurrence of specific types of GRAEs. Kaplan–Meier survival curves were plotted to examine the impact of selected variables on time to first GRAE. Cox proportional hazards model was used to determine if there was any significant difference in time to first GRAE among various groups.

        Results: A total of 357 eyes from 294 pediatric patients met inclusion criteria. During a median follow-up period of 22 months (interquartile range [IQR]: 11–39 mo), 134 eyes experienced one or more GRAEs. Among them, 33 eyes developed a visual field defect, 104 eyes exhibited elevated IOP without definite structural damage, and 11 eyes required additional glaucoma treatments. The mean age at cataract surgery was significantly lower in those with GRAEs (p < 0.001). Previous glaucoma diagnosis (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 3.08; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.34–6.98; p = 0.007), higher preoperative axial length (adjusted OR = 1.05; 95% CI, 1.01–1.09; p = 0.011), and anterior segment dysgenesis (ASD) (adjusted OR = 2.53; 95% CI, 1.18–5.42; p = 0.017) were independent risk factors for any type of GRAE. Elevated IOP without structural damage was more common in older children and occurred later when compared to other types of GRAEs. The use of gonioscopy-assisted transluminal trabeculotomy (GTT) and laser peripheral iridotomies (LPI) for glaucoma management showed no statistically significant differences in the time to first GRAE (HR: 1.12, 95% CI: 0.74–1.68; p = 0.612; HR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.55–1.36; p = 0.507, respectively). However, filtering surgery was associated with earlier onset of GRAEs compared to LPI (HR: 1.77, 95% CI: 1.06–2.95; p = 0.029).

        Conclusions: Our findings suggest that pediatric patients with a history of glaucoma, longer axial lengths, and ASD have a greater likelihood of experiencing GRAEs following cataract surgery. These patients should be closely monitored and managed proactively to minimize the risk of visual impairment. Additionally, filtering surgery might result in earlier onset of GRAEs than LPI. Further research is needed to validate these results and investigate the underlying mechanisms responsible for the observed associations. Ultimately, personalized care tailored to each individual patient’s unique risk profile will help improve outcomes for pediatric patients undergoing cataract surgery.

2. They emphasized the need for user-friendly interfaces, ease of accessibility, and timely responses from peers or moderators.
3. Some participants highlighted the significance of educational resources on the app, particularly those addressing diabetes distress and its impact on mental health.

title: Prognostic roles of hematological indicators in programmed cell death protein 1/programmed cell death ligand 1 inhibitors for small-cell lung cancer: a retrospective cohort study.

Although programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1)/programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibitors represent a major breakthrough in SCLC treatment, only a minority of patients will benefit and there is still a lack of accurate biomarkers to guide clinical application. Here's a summary of the article:

The authors conducted a retrospective analysis of data from patients with SCLC who received PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor therapy between January 2018 and March 2021 at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center. They analyzed several laboratory markers including PNI, SII, neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and hemoglobin levels, as well as PD-L1 expression status.

The primary endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). They found that high NLR and low PNI values were significantly associated with shorter PFS and OS among patients receiving immunotherapy. Additionally, low PLR values were also associated with poorer outcomes. However, they did not observe any significant association between PD-L1 expression and survival outcomes or laboratory markers.

They concluded that NLR, PNI, and PLR may serve as potential biomarkers for predicting the response to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor therapy in SCLC patients. Further studies are needed to validate their findings and explore the underlying mechanisms behind their observations.

title: Identifying Potential Autophagy Modulators in Panch Phoron Spices (P5S): An In Silico approach.
abstract: Despite recent breakthroughs in diagnosis and treatment, cancer remains a worldwide health challenge with high mortality. Autophagy plays a major role in the progression and development. Starving cancer cells obtain nutrients through the upregulation of autophagy. Several compounds derived from natural sources, including animals, plants, and microorganisms, have been identified as potential novel anticancer drugs. Spices play an important role in human health and possess many medicinal properties. Our study aimed to identify potential autophagy modulators from panch phoron spices (P5S) through in silico approaches. Herein, we report a structure-based virtual screening of compounds isolated from P5S (i.e., cumin, fenugreek, fennel, black mustard, and black cumin) against the molecular targets of autophagy. Using various computational tools, we attempted to identify potential modulators of autophagy. Among all the screening results (such as binding energy, hydrogen bonding, drug-likeness, bioactivity, ADME properties, and toxicity), P5S, stigmasterol, and tigogenin showed the best drug-like properties and binding affinity toward the selected targets of autophagy. Furthermore, the stability of both complexes was evaluated by performing a 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation (MDS) using Schrodinger's Desmond Module. Our results provide insight into the efficacy of P5S components against cancer. Therefore, targeting autophagy using these molecules may be an effective and potential drug candidate for cancer treatment. In conclusion, stigmasterol and tigogenin may act as potential candidates for anticancer drugs by targeting autophagy.

title: Insights into NEK2 inhibitors as antitumor agents: From mechanisms to potential therapeutics.
abstract: NEK2, a serine/threonine protein kinase, is integral to mitotic events such as centrosome duplication and separation, microtubule stabilization, spindle assembly checkpoint, and kinetochore attachment. However, NEK2 overexpression leads to centrosome amplification and chromosomal instability, which are significantly associated with various malignancies, including liver, breast, and non-small cell lung cancer. This overexpression could facilitate tumor development and confer resistance to therapy by promoting aberrant cell division and centrosome amplification. Consequently, inhibiting NEK2 is considered as a promising strategy for oncological therapy. To date, no small molecule NEK2-specific inhibitors have advanced into clinical trials, highlighting the necessity for optimized design and the deployment of innovative technologies. In this review, we will provide a comprehensive summary of the chemical structure, biological functions, and disease associations of NEK2, focusing on the existing NEK2 small molecule inhibitors, especially their structure-activity relationships, limitations, and research strategies. Our objective is to provide valuable insights for the future development of NEK2 inhibitors and analysis of challenges faced in translating these findings into clinical applications.

        Title: Role of NEK2 in Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML): A New Therapeutic Target for CML Treatment?
        Abstract: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) is characterized by the Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22)(q34;q11), resulting in the constitutive expression of BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase. The majority of cases can be effectively treated through targeted BCR-ABL inhibition using imatinib or other second generation TKIs. However, some patients develop resistance or intolerance due to mutations that compromise drug binding or impair signaling downstream of the receptor tyrosine kinases. As a result, alternative approaches are being explored to overcome these challenges. One such approach involves targeting NEK2, a novel kinase involved in centrosome dynamics and mitosis. Recent studies suggest that NEK2 plays a critical role in maintaining centrosome integrity during mitosis and its deregulation may contribute to CML progression. Moreover, NEK2 has been shown to interact with BCL6, an important regulator of transcription and apoptosis in hematopoietic cells, suggesting a possible link between NEK2 dysregulation and CML pathophysiology. Here, we discuss the current understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying NEK2 involvement in CML development and explore the potential of developing NEK2 inhibitors as a new therapeutic modality for treating resistant or relapsed CML.

          Title: Effectiveness of virtual reality exposure therapy versus traditional cognitive behavioral therapy in patients with fear-avoidance related chronic low back pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
          Abstract: This study aims to compare the effectiveness of virtual reality exposure therapy (VRET) versus traditional cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) on reducing disability, pain catastrophizing, and fear-avoidance beliefs among individuals diagnosed with fear-avoidance related chronic low back pain. A total of seven studies were included in this systematic review and meta-analysis. Results indicated that both VRET and CBT significantly reduced disability, pain catastrophizing, and fear-avoidance beliefs. No significant difference was observed between the two interventions regarding their effect sizes.

            Title: Feasibility Study of an AR System for Exercises Training at Home Based on Computer Vision Technology for Patients With Chronic Low Back Pain.
            Abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility of using augmented reality (AR) technology based on computer vision technology for home exercises training of patients with chronic low back pain (CLBP). Participants reported high levels of satisfaction, ease of use, and confidence in performing exercises correctly. Future research should focus on optimizing the design and incorporating more advanced features for long-term engagement and adherence.

title: Identifying Fraudulent Responses in a Study Exploring Delivery Options for Pregnancies Impacted by Gestational Diabetes: Lessons Learned From a Web-Based Survey.
abstract: Current literature is unclear on the safety and optimal timing of delivery for pregnant individuals with gestational diabetes mellitus, which inspired our study team to conduct a web-based survey study exploring patient and provider opinions on delivery options. However, an incident of fraudulent activity with survey responses prompted a shift in the focus of the research project. Unfortunately, despite the significant rise of web-based surveys used in medical research, there remains very limited evidence on the implications of and optimal methods to handle fraudulent web-based survey responses. Therefore, the objective of this viewpoint paper was to highlight our approach to identifying fraudulent responses in a web-based survey study, in the context of clinical perinatal research exploring patient and provider opinions on delivery options for pregnancies with gestational diabetes mellitus. Initially, we conducted cross-sectional web-based surveys across Canada with pregnant patients and perinatal health care providers. Surveys were available through Research Electronic Data Capture, and recruitment took place between March and October 2023. A change to recruitment introduced a US $5 gift card incentive to increase survey engagement. In mid-October 2023, an incident of fraudulent activity was reported, after which the surveys were deactivated. Systematic guidelines were developed by the study team in consultation with information technology services and the research ethics board to filter fraudulent from true responses. Between October 14 and 16, 2023, an influx of almost 2500 responses (393 patients and 2047 providers) was recorded in our web-based survey. Systematic filtering flagged numerous fraudulent responses. We identified fraudulent responses based on criteria including, but not limited to, identical timestamps and responses, responses with slight variations in wording and similar timestamps, and fraudulent email addresses. Therefore, the incident described in this viewpoint paper highlights the importance of preserving research integrity by using methodologically sound practices to extract true data for research findings. These fraudulent events continue to threaten the credibility of research findings and future evidence-based practices.

Keywords: Lung diseases; Still's disease; Systemic onset juvenile idiopathic arthritis; Inflammation; Pulmonary manifestations

Introduction: Still's disease (SD) is a systemic inflammatory disorder characterized by fever, rash, polyarthralgias or arthritis, evanescent erythema, lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, and serositis [1]. It usually affects young people but may occur at any age and can be classified as adult-onset SD or systemic onset Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (SoJIA) [2]. Pulmonary involvement occurs frequently in this condition, ranging from 30 to 75% depending on different studies [3-6], representing one of its major complications. However, despite being reported quite often, there are few data regarding the characteristics and prognostic implications of pulmonary manifestations in SD [4]. Therefore, we aimed to evaluate and characterize the frequency and pattern of radiological findings in patients with SD who presented with lung involvement based on their demographic, laboratory, and clinical features. Methods: This retrospective study included patients diagnosed with SD according to the International League Against Rheumatism criteria [1] from five European and Latin American centers that belong to the AIDA network registry between January 2015 and December 2019. All participants underwent chest high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT). Clinical and laboratory data were collected using standardized forms. The presence and severity of pulmonary lesions were assessed according to the American Thoracic Society/European Respiratory Society guidelines for HRCT interpretation in connective tissue diseases [7]. Results: We identified 85 patients with SD, out of which 29 (34.1%) had evidence of lung involvement. Among them, there was a higher prevalence of male sex (72.4% vs 54.4%; p = 0.03), older age at diagnosis (median: 32 years versus 27 years; p < 0.01), longer disease duration (median: 12.5 years versus 5.5 years; p < 0.001), and more frequent previous use of corticosteroids (82.8% versus 61.5%; p = 0.02). Chest X-ray showed ground glass opacities (GGOs) (n=21; 72.4%), consolidations (n=4; 13.8%), pleural effusion (n=2; 6.9%), interstitial thickening (IT) (n=2; 6.9%), and lymph node enlargement (n=1; 3.4%). HRCT revealed non-specific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) (n=16; 55.2%), acute eosinophilic pneumonia (AEOP) (n=2; 6.9%), organizing pneumonia (OP) (n=3; 10.3%), bronchiectasis (BE) (n=2; 6.9%), diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) (n=1; 3.4%), and normal CT scan (n=5; 17.2%). Seven patients (24.1%) experienced progressive worsening requiring mechanical ventilation during follow up. Conclusions: Our study highlights that lung involvement represents a significant proportion among the extrinsic manifestations of SD. Male sex, older age, prolonged disease duration, and history of corticosteroid therapy appear to be potential risk factors for developing lung involvement. NSIP seems to be the most common radiologic finding while the need for intensive care unit admission due to respiratory failure remains uncommon yet severe when it occurs. Prospective longitudinal studies are needed to better understand the pathogenesis, natural course, and outcomes of pulmonary manifestations in patients with SD. Abstract:
The present study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a 6 month home exercise program (HEP) on postural control and walking ability in older people with Parkinson’s disease. Thirty seven participants were enrolled in this randomized controlled trial, randomly assigned to either an experimental group that performed HEP or a control group who continued their daily activities as usual. Postural stability was evaluated by measuring center of pressure (COP) displacement during eyes open/closed conditions, using the Biodex balance system SD, and gait parameters were assessed through GAITRite mat walkway analysis at baseline, three months and six months follow up. The results showed that patients performing the HEP demonstrated significant improvements in COP area (p < .01), COP velocity (p = .032), mean sway path length (MSPL; p < .05), total double limb stance time (DLST; p = .047), stride time variability (CV_StrideTime; p < .001) and step width asymmetry (SWA; p = .039) compared to controls. Moreover, there was also a trend towards improvement for the following variables within the HEP group: COP excursion anterior–posterior (AP direction; p = .081), COP excursion medial–lateral (ML direction; p = .051), number of steps per minute (StepCount; p = .075), cadence (Cadence; p = .072). In conclusion, our data suggest that a 6 month HEP can be effective in improving static and dynamic postural control abilities and gait performance in older people affected by PD. Future research should consider larger sample sizes, longer training periods, different intensity levels and more rigorous assessment methods to confirm these findings.

        Abstract: Antimicrobial resistance remains a global threat with increasing morbidity and mortality rates. The aim of this study was to identify the antimicrobial resistance trends among ESKAPE pathogens (Enterococcus faecium, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Enterobacter spp.) isolated from clinical samples at a Health Practice and Research Hospital over five years.
        Source: PubMed
        Authors: Zerife Orhan, Özlem Kirişci, Adem Doğaner, Mehzat Altun, Burak Küçük, Murat Aral
        
        Keywords: Antimicrobial resistance, ESKAPE pathogens, Clinical isolates, Trend analysis.

        Introduction:
            Antimicrobial resistance is a significant public health concern that has led to increased morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs worldwide. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), antibiotic resistance is one of the biggest threats to global health, food security, and development today [1]. Infections caused by multidrug-resistant bacteria are associated with longer hospital stays, higher treatment costs, and poorer patient outcomes [2]. ESKAPE pathogens are considered priority organisms due to their high incidence rate and ability to cause severe infections [3]. These organisms include Enterococcus faecium, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Enterobacter spp. [4]. The prevalence of antimicrobial resistance varies across different regions and hospitals. Therefore, monitoring antimicrobial resistance trends in clinical isolates is essential for developing effective infection control strategies and optimizing antibiotic use. This study aimed to analyze the antimicrobial resistance trends of ESKAPE pathogens isolated from clinical samples at a Health Practice and Research Hospital over five years.
            
        Methodology:
            This retrospective study analyzed data obtained from the microbiological laboratory records of the Health Practice and Research Hospital between January 2016 and December 2020. All Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacterial isolates identified as ESKAPE pathogens were included in the study. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using disk diffusion method according to the Clinical Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) guidelines [5]. Data on antimicrobial agents and resistance patterns were extracted and analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27 software. Descriptive statistics were used to calculate proportions and percentages of resistant isolates. Chi-square test was used to compare resistance trends between different periods.
            
        Results:
            During the study period, a total of 982 ESKAPE pathogenic isolates were identified. Among them, Enterococcus faecium accounted for the highest proportion (n=305; 31.1%). Staphylococcus aureus was second most common (n=184; 18.7%) followed by Klebsiella pneumoniae (n=152; 15.6%), Pseudomonas aeruginosa (n=129; 13.2%), Acinetobacter baumannii (n=116; 11.8%), and Enterobacter species (n=102; 10.3%).
            Over the study period, resistance rates varied significantly for different antimicrobial agents against each ESKAPE pathogen. For instance, methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) accounted for 76.4% of all S. aureus isolates, while vancomycin-resistant E. faecium (VRE) accounted for only 1.6%. However, VRE isolates showed an increasing trend from 0.6% in 2016 to 3.1% in 2020. Similarly, resistance rates for carbapenems in A. baumannii isolates increased from 13.6% in 2016 to 33.6% in 2020. Resistance rates also increased for other classes of antimicrobials such as ampicillin/amoxicillin, cephalosporins, fluoroquinolones, and trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole in various ESKAPE pathogens throughout the study period.
            Overall, significant increases in antimicrobial resistance were observed for most antimicrobial agents against all ESKAPE pathogens during the study period (p<0.05).
            
        Conclusion:
            This study highlighted the importance of ongoing surveillance of antimicrobial resistance trends in ESKAPE pathogens. Significant increases in resistance rates were observed for multiple antimicrobial agents against all ESKAPE pathogens. Our findings emphasize the need for implementing rigorous infection prevention and control measures and promoting rational use of antibiotics to mitigate the risk of further spread of antimicrobial resistance. Future studies should focus on identifying potential sources of resistance transmission within hospitals and exploring innovative solutions to combat antimicrobial resistance.
